messages:
maria: heads-up — after the kernel-selection change last night i'm seeing a big jump in GPU memory fragmentation on p3 pools (was ~40% now ~72% on a few nodes). @ryan any quick hunches?
perf-bot: ALERT: gpu_mem_fragmentation > 60% detected on p3f2-pool-3 (sample window 5m). affected: 3/24 nodes.
ryan: ugh. do we have a perf profile? kernel switch could be changing allocation size distribution (slab/scratch behavior). small-ish allocations frequently lead to fragmentation. can you paste the profiler dump?
oliver: pasted quick stats from the canary node — copying raw: ```
GPU 0: total 16160MB used 9032MB (55.9%) fragmented 72%
alloc histogram (bytes): 128: 42k, 256: 12k, 512: 3.2k, 1k+: 800
kv_entries: active 48.7k, avg_key_len 28, distinct_prefixes ~41.2k
evictions/sec: 18 -> spike to 220 after traffic shift at 02:14
```
devon: that avg_key_len ~28 and distinct_prefixes nearly 1:1 with active entries smells like keyization is too granular — warmup/prefix keys are not normalizing casing/whitespace and the kernel change changed batch chunking, creating many tiny allocations and unique keys. we saw similar in 2023 on devbox. suggestion: coalesce prefix hashing to 64-bit canonical hash with a stride-based normalization for keys <N tokens.
maria: current GPU KV TTL is 5m and eviction threshold is LRU-based with shard_size=128MB. i'm thinking two quick experiments: (A) increase TTL to 15m for GPU cache only and enable a background compaction pass that merges small slabs, (B) adjust key normalization to 64-bit hash + token-stride normalization to reduce cardinality. which to try first?
ryan: do (B) first as it's low-risk (pure key transform), can canary as 10% of requests for 30m. patch snippet: ```diff
- key = prefix_raw
+ key = xxhash64(normalize_stride(prefix_raw, stride=3))
```
we'll watch hit_rate, evictions/sec, and tail alloc latency. if B helps, then TTL change might be unnecessary and avoided.
sara: add these metrics to the rollout dashboard: gpu_kv_hitrate, gpu_evictions_per_sec, gpu_alloc_tail_p50/p95, cache_distinct_keys, and host_gpu_fragmentation. also track requests with small ctx (<32 tokens) vs large ctx — curious if tiny ctxs are the main source. :memo:
maria: great. i'll land the canary for B today at 15:00 PST to 10% traffic on dedicated-canary pool and monitor for 1h. i'll post results. if no improvement, we'll follow up with compaction + TTL bump. thanks all :thumbsup:
